# The table contract — tabular output from pcrec commands

<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document states the wire format every pcrec command that outputs a DATA
TABLE obeys. It is the contract: present tense, normative. Its history is
`docs/dev/history/table_contract_record.md`, which is not normative. The
column sets of the individual tables are not here: `docs/spec/registry.md`
states those of the syntax, verb, family, axis and definition registries, and each other
producer's document states its own (§1).

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. Scope

<a id="s1-p1"></a>[1¶1] Every pcrec command whose output is a data table conforms. A new tabular
command conforms from the day it exists; one that does not is a defect.

| command | table | producer shape |
|---|---|---|
| `--list-syntax` | the syntax construct registry | one anonymous table |
| `--list-verbs` | the `(*VERB)` name table | one anonymous table |
| `--list-definitions` | the replacement/definition table | one anonymous table |
| `--list-families` | the construct-family index | one anonymous table |
| `--list-axes` | the optimization-axis registry | an anonymous main table, then the named section `memfn` (the search-code kit's option registry, `registry.md` §6) |
| `--list-limits` | the numeric-limits table | one anonymous table |
| `--list-source` | the `.rxt` source file, as written (`rxt_format.md` §2) | an anonymous main table, then up to four named sections: `provenance`, `variants`, `cases`, `aux` — each emitted only when non-empty, always after the main table |
| `--list-schema` | the `.rxt` format's own schema (`rxt_format.md` §1.13) | two named sections, `schema` and `surface` |
| `--emit-ir` | the VM program listing (`docs/spec/ir_listing.md` §3) | nine named sections, no anonymous table; the sections have different column counts |
| `--emit-facts` | the pattern-facts record listing (`docs/spec/facts_listing.md` §4) | two named sections, `facts` and `decisions` |
| `--list-analyses` | the analyses built into the library (`docs/spec/findings.md`) | one anonymous table |
| `--list-analysis` | what one analysis name, or each target of one `.rxt` file, resolves to (`docs/spec/findings.md`) | every table a named section: `chain`, `resolution`, one per data kind, `declarations`, `provenance`; or `targets`, `chain`, `resolution` |

<a id="s1-p2"></a>[1¶2] `--list-analysis`'s free-text columns — `question`, `reader`, `analyzer`, a
provenance `value` and a `location` path — pass through §2¶5's
escaping (`pcrec_sb_text`: a TAB or control byte becomes `\xNN`), because a
user bundle's prose may carry a TAB; its hex `key` and decimal `count`
columns need none by grammar.

<a id="s1-p3"></a>[1¶3] `--trace` is not in scope: its output is an event stream from an
instrumented matcher, not a table. A future trace mode that emits a table
conforms for that table.

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. The producer contract

1. <a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] Output is TAB-separated values, one row per record, `\n` line ends.
2. <a id="s2-p2"></a>[2¶2] Lines beginning `#` are COMMENTS: free prose, ignored by parsers.
3. <a id="s2-p3"></a>[2¶3] The LAST `#` line before the first data row is the HEADER: `#` followed
   immediately by the column names, tab-separated, in on-the-wire order
   (`#kind<TAB>selector<TAB>syntax<TAB>…`).
4. <a id="s2-p4"></a>[2¶4] Columns are APPENDED ONLY: never inserted, renamed, removed or reordered.
   A new column lands after the last existing one, with a `#` comment line
   above the header describing it.
5. <a id="s2-p5"></a>[2¶5] An empty field means "none"; a field never contains a TAB (which is what
   makes §2¶1 checkable per row).

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. The consumer contract

1. <a id="s3-p1"></a>[3¶1] Resolve columns BY HEADER NAME, never by hardcoded field count and never
   by bare position. An awk consumer builds a name-to-index map from the
   header row; a C consumer reads the header line first.
2. <a id="s3-p2"></a>[3¶2] Unknown trailing columns MUST be ignored. Trailing-safety is what
   §2¶4 buys; a consumer that breaks on an appended column has
   violated this contract.
3. <a id="s3-p3"></a>[3¶3] A consumer MAY assert the field count only as EQUALITY WITH THE HEADER's
   declared count (an integrity check that no TAB leaked into a field),
   never as a literal number.

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. Sections

<a id="s4-p1"></a>[4¶1] Multi-table output — one command's output holding several tables with
different columns — uses sections.

1. <a id="s4-p2"></a>[4¶2] A section is announced by a SECTION line: `#section NAME` (a `#` line
   whose first word is `section`; NAME is a bare word, the section's stable
   address). It is followed by that section's own comments and its own
   HEADER line (§2¶3 applies per section: the last `#` line
   before a section's data is that section's header), then its data rows,
   until the next `#section` line or end of output.
2. <a id="s4-p3"></a>[4¶3] Output with no `#section` line is a single anonymous section: a
   sectionless table read under §2 and §3 alone. A single-table dump may
   stay anonymous.
3. <a id="s4-p4"></a>[4¶4] Section NAMES are the API: append-only as a set (a name, once shipped,
   keeps its meaning; new sections may be added), and each section's columns
   follow §2 independently (append-only within the section).
4. <a id="s4-p5"></a>[4¶5] A section-aware consumer SELECTS its section by name and parses within it
   under §3. A consumer reading a multi-section stream without selecting
   MUST fail loudly rather than parse rows across section boundaries.
5. <a id="s4-p6"></a>[4¶6] The LEADING ANONYMOUS TABLE of a stream whose main table stays unnamed
   while named sections follow it (`--list-source`, `--list-axes`) is
   selected as every line BEFORE the first `#section` line; the result is a
   sectionless table. A consumer that reads "every non-`#` line" without that
   cut reads the sections' rows as the main table's. The shell
   implementation is `tests/lib/table.sh`'s `table_main`.
6. <a id="s4-p7"></a>[4¶7] Tables of equal standing in one stream are all named: an anonymous first
   section is the one table no conforming consumer can select. Only a main
   table that precedes appended sections (`--list-source`, `--list-axes`)
   may stay unnamed; a stream of peers (`--list-schema`, `--emit-ir`,
   `--emit-facts`) has no anonymous table.
7. <a id="s4-p8"></a>[4¶8] A `#` comment after a section's header line and before its first row is
   read as that section's header (§2¶3, applied per section). A section
   whose population can be empty therefore ends at its header line when it
   is empty (`--list-axes`' `memfn` section) or states the emptiness as a
   data row (`--emit-ir`, `docs/spec/ir_listing.md`), never as a trailing
   comment.

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. The checks

1. <a id="s5-p1"></a>[5¶1] HEADER TRUTHFULNESS: every data row's field count equals its header's
   declared count, per section. `tests/lib/table.sh`'s
   `table_check_truthfulness` is the one implementation; every producer's
   suite calls it.
2. <a id="s5-p2"></a>[5¶2] GENERATOR AGREEMENT: any checker that carries its own column list (the
   column list in `tests/registry/compliance_section.py`) cross-checks it
   against the emitted header, so the generator and its checker cannot
   disagree silently.
